domain_label: Knowledge-Graph Relation Validation — Owner-Gated Repair Proposals & Provenance of Machine Corrections (propose-never-rewrite typed operations — reverse / retype / negate / delete / add / merge — surfaced only as human-approvable proposals, each carrying a PROV-O trail of agent, activity, and source evidence, with the honesty tag surviving until a human confirms it)
purpose: The repair-and-provenance layer of the kgverify specialist: how a relation-validation authority turns a verified truth verdict (from kb2) into an OWNER-GATED, typed repair PROPOSAL that is never silently applied, and records every accepted correction as an immutable PROV-O provenance trail rather than a bare mutation. It defines the typed operations (reverse — the exact fix for the D1 inversion; retype; negate; delete; add; merge), the human-in-the-loop accept/reject loop with rollback and branching, the rule that a human-verified correction dominates any automatic one, and the honesty discipline that a machine-corrected edge stays ESTIMATE until a human confirms it FACT — never laundered by the act of correction. It owns repair-proposal discipline and correction provenance, not the truth verdict (kb2), the deterministic detection (kb1), the graph schema (kgraph), or the render (viz).
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all base metric scores are heuristic priors and every design call is an ESTIMATE synthesized from the cited literature and app grounding files

external method claims are grounded in published work and carried inline as [FACT-source: URL]; publisher pages returned 403 to direct fetch (bot-block, not a proxy failure), so citations rest on search-engine summaries that quote those papers and any figure not directly quoted is left unstated rather than invented

the propose-never-rewrite law, the typed CRUD-with-review operations, and the human-in-the-loop accept/reject loop are grounded in CleanGraph and HITL-workflow literature; the specific app UI and store are the fixed target this KB specifies discipline for, not implements

provenance is modelled with W3C PROV-O (Entity/Activity/Agent) and statement-level (RDF-star) / PAV authoring axes; whether the app persists provenance in exactly this form is a session UNKNOWN to confirm by recon, with the record's required fields specified regardless

this KB is the OWNER-GATED REPAIR & PROVENANCE third of the kgverify specialist; deterministic detection (kb1) and calibrated content verification (kb2) are neighboring KBs this one consumes verdicts from and turns into gated, provenance-stamped proposals
exclusions: the deterministic logical/mereological detection that raises candidate defects (kb1) and the calibrated content-truth verdict (kb2) beyond consuming their typed output as the basis of a proposal

all graph SCHEMA/STRUCTURE governance — whether a proposed reverse/retype/add is a legal edge, per-type directionality, DAG acyclicity, closed-vocabulary or new-relation-type changes, node granularity (owned by kgraph); kgverify states the semantic need, kgraph governs the schema
the render of a correction status, a negated edge, or a proposal UI's visual encoding (owned by viz) and the mastery/scheduling math (owned by learner/sched)

building the correction store, the diff/rollback engine, or the approval UI in the app (owned by app engineering/extint) beyond specifying the operations, the gating discipline, and the provenance record such code must implement
authoring the source content or the terminology catalog (owned by contenteng) beyond recording which source evidence a correction was derived from

glossary.definition: The governing law: refinement is done through interactive acceptance or rejection of model-sourced corrections, 'reducing manual error correction cost while maintaining expert control,' with explicit approval mechanisms at each refinement step preventing silent overwrites [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03932 (CleanGraph)]; the live graph is mutated only by an approved action.

The CleanGraph CRUD-with-review operation set: add edge, delete edge, reverse edge direction (the exact fix for D1's inversion), merge duplicate nodes, retype relation, and negate — each surfaced as a suggested modification a human acknowledges and acts on, with rollback/branching for comparing alternative interventions [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03932].

A modular loop of detection → feedback elicitation → adaptation → quality control, escalating on 'changes, failures, or model uncertainty' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/human-in-the-loop-workflow ; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030645732500086X]; a human-verified correction dominates any automatic one, paralleling kgraph's human-verified-link dominance.

Every accepted correction is recorded, not merely applied: provenance is 'the set of annotations that describe the origin of statements: who asserted them, from which source they were derived, when and how they were produced, and under which conditions they hold' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.15246].

W3C PROV-O (Entity/Activity/Agent) applied to a correction so each edit records the correcting agent (which model), the activity (verify/repair), and the source evidence [FACT-source: https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/ ; https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/].

What a repair log needs provenance for: it 'support[s] assessments of trust, reliability, and accountability by linking claims to sources and agents… enables versioning and change tracking, making it possible to record corrections, retractions, and refinements over time' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.15246 ; https://www.utwente.nl/en/eemcs/fois2024/resources/papers/dibowski-full-traceability-and-provenance-for-knowledge-graphs.pdf].

Statement-level provenance via RDF-star so a single corrected edge carries its own trail without polluting siblings [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.15246 ; https://www.utwente.nl/en/eemcs/fois2024/resources/papers/dibowski-full-traceability-and-provenance-for-knowledge-graphs.pdf], with authoring/versioning axes (who, derived-from, version) via PAV [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1304.7224].

A machine-corrected edge is stamped ESTIMATE (LLM-inferred, evidence-linked) until a human confirms it FACT — never laundered into FACT by the act of correction; unverifiable claims stay UNKNOWN and quarantined (inherits kgraph's evidence-label policy verbatim).

Prefer traceable validation whose verdict points at the retrieved document chunk [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07507], so a reviewer accepts or rejects a correction on the evidence, not on the model's say-so.

A batch correction run is staged as a reviewable branch with rollback, not a live bulk edit [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03932], so many edges can be compared and reverted before any is committed.

The correction record (agent, activity, source, timestamp, prior value) is immutable and append-only [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/ ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.15246], so a reviewer can audit corrections, retractions and refinements over time without a prior value being overwritten.

nodes.definition: Frame the layer: this KB is the OWNER-GATED REPAIR & PROVENANCE third of kgverify — it turns a verified truth verdict (from kb2, over a candidate defect from kb1) into a typed repair PROPOSAL that a human explicitly accepts or rejects, and records every accepted correction as an immutable provenance trail rather than a bare mutation. Feature A specifies exactly this: 'proposes corrections; never silently rewrites; owner-gated; machine-corrected edges carry an honesty tag and provenance' [FACT-source: NEW_FEATURES_PLAN §3A]. The payoff is that a correction is safe (nothing changes without approval) and auditable (every change traces to an agent, activity, and source); the discipline is that this layer owns the proposal and the provenance, not the truth verdict (kb2), the detection (kb1), the schema (kgraph), or the render (viz) [ESTIMATE — design synthesis, high confidence].

included: turns a kb2 verdict into an owner-gated typed proposal
records every accepted correction as an immutable provenance trail
owns proposal + provenance, not truth/detection/schema/render

nodes.definition: State the governing law: PROPOSE, never silently rewrite. Refinement is done through interactive acceptance or rejection of model-sourced corrections, 'reducing manual error correction cost while maintaining expert control,' with 'explicit approval mechanisms at each refinement step' preventing silent overwrites [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03932 (CleanGraph)]. The live graph is mutated ONLY by an approved action; a verdict from kb2 — however confident — becomes a proposal, not an edit. This is the load-bearing discipline of the whole specialist: it is why kgverify is a verification-and-repair-proposal authority rather than a delete/rewrite pass, and it is what protects the graph from a confidently-wrong machine correction being applied before a human sees it.

nodes.definition: Define the typed repair operations, mirroring CleanGraph's CRUD-with-review: add edge, delete edge, REVERSE edge direction, MERGE duplicate nodes, RETYPE relation, and NEGATE — each surfaced as a suggested modification a human acknowledges and acts on, with rollback/branching for comparing alternative interventions [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03932]. Each operation is typed so the proposal is explicit about WHAT would change (reverse the pituitary/adrenal part_of; retype related→causal; negate a contradicted edge; merge two duplicate nodes), and each maps to a kb1 defect class and a kb2 verdict. The operation set is closed and auditable — a correction is always one of these named operations with its before/after state, never an ad-hoc edit.

nodes.definition: Structure the human-in-the-loop as a modular loop: detection → feedback elicitation → adaptation → quality control, escalating on 'changes, failures, or model uncertainty' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/human-in-the-loop-workflow ; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030645732500086X (KG validation integrating LLMs + HITL)]. Detection is kb1+kb2's typed candidate/verdict; feedback is the owner's accept/reject on a proposal; adaptation records the outcome and can update thresholds; quality control audits the accepted corrections. The loop escalates precisely where autonomy is least safe — a low-confidence verdict, a flag-vs-evidence conflict, or a calibration-drift signal all raise the case to a human rather than resolving automatically. This is the operational shape of propose-never-rewrite.

nodes.definition: Fix the tie-break: a HUMAN-verified correction dominates any automatic one. When an owner's decision and a machine proposal disagree — the owner rejects a high-confidence fix, or accepts against the model — the human decision is authoritative and is recorded as such, paralleling kgraph's 'a human-verified link dominates any automatic one'. This dominance is asymmetric on purpose: the machine can propose but never override a human, and a human can override the machine at any confidence. It is the ultimate guarantee behind propose-never-rewrite — even a perfectly-calibrated, evidence-grounded verdict yields to the owner, because the owner bears the consequence of a wrong study-graph edge.

included: human-verified correction dominates any automatic one
asymmetric: machine proposes, human overrides at any confidence
parallels kgraph's human-verified-link dominance
excluded: the accept/reject loop mechanics (its own node)

nodes.definition: Treat every accepted correction as a provenance RECORD, not a bare mutation. Provenance is 'the set of annotations that describe the origin of statements: who asserted them, from which source they were derived, when and how they were produced, and under which conditions they hold' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.15246]. So accepting the D1 reversal does not just flip the edge — it writes a record of who accepted it, which model proposed it, which source evidence backed it, when, and under what verdict. This turns the graph's history into an auditable ledger rather than a sequence of opaque state changes, and it is what lets a later reviewer understand and, if needed, retract any machine-influenced edge.

nodes.definition: State what the provenance trail is FOR, because it is exactly what a repair log needs: provenance 'support[s] assessments of trust, reliability, and accountability by linking claims to sources and agents… enables versioning and change tracking, making it possible to record corrections, retractions, and refinements over time' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.15246 ; https://www.utwente.nl/en/eemcs/fois2024/resources/papers/dibowski-full-traceability-and-provenance-for-knowledge-graphs.pdf]. These functions are why the record is immutable and append-only (next nodes).

nodes.definition: Attach provenance at the RIGHT granularity: per-assertion, via RDF-star / statement-level provenance so a single corrected edge carries its OWN trail without polluting siblings [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.15246 ; https://www.utwente.nl/en/eemcs/fois2024/resources/papers/dibowski-full-traceability-and-provenance-for-knowledge-graphs.pdf], with authoring/versioning axes (who, derived-from, version) via PAV [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1304.7224]. This matters because a correction touches one edge, not the whole graph: the D1 reversal's trail must live on that edge alone, so an audit of the pituitary/adrenal edge does not drag in unrelated corrections and a rollback reverts exactly one assertion. Per-assertion granularity is what makes the ledger precise rather than a coarse global changelog.

dominance_rules.rule: Honesty-tag survival dominates the convenience of marking a fix done
dominance_rules.rationale: a machine correction is an inference until a human confirms it
dominance_rules.trigger: a corrected edge's status is about to be raised
dominance_rules.action: keep it ESTIMATE until human-confirmed FACT; keep UNKNOWN quarantined

dominance_rules.rule: The kb2 verdict dominates the defect's surface shape in choosing the operation
dominance_rules.rationale: an inversion surface can mislead toward a reverse when the truth needs a retype
dominance_rules.trigger: a repair operation is being selected
dominance_rules.action: choose the operation from kb2's verdict (D1 is retype, not reverse)

dominance_rules.rule: Reviewable-branch staging dominates live bulk apply
dominance_rules.rationale: a systematic model error can sweep the whole graph in one unreviewed pass
dominance_rules.trigger: a batch correction run is proposed
dominance_rules.action: stage it as a branch with rollback and per-proposal review

dominance_rules.rule: Immutable append-only recording dominates in-place edits of the trail
dominance_rules.rationale: versioning, rollback and audit require the prior value to be preserved
dominance_rules.trigger: a correction, retraction, or confirmation is recorded
dominance_rules.action: append a new record; never overwrite the prior one

dominance_rules.rationale: a reviewer must decide on the evidence, not the model's assertion
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposal is surfaced for review
dominance_rules.action: carry the retrieved evidence chunk into the proposal

dominance_rules.rule: kgraph's schema authority dominates kb3's repair when a proposal implies a schema change
dominance_rules.rationale: kb3 owns the proposal, not whether the resulting edge is legal
dominance_rules.trigger: a reverse/retype/add would change the schema or vocabulary
dominance_rules.action: hand the schema legality to kgraph; kb3 only proposes and records

anti_rework_rules.rule: Establish propose-never-rewrite and no-auto-apply before any correction path is built
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a silent-rewrite path that must later be walked back after it applies a wrong fix

anti_rework_rules.rule: Express every correction as a typed operation with a before/after from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: ad-hoc edits that cannot be audited, compared, or rolled back

anti_rework_rules.rule: Choose the repair operation from the kb2 verdict, not the defect surface shape
anti_rework_rules.prevents: mis-fixing D1 with a naive reverse instead of the correct retype

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the PROV-O trail and honesty tag at the moment of acceptance
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a corrected edge with no provenance or a laundered fact-status that must later be reconstructed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record corrections immutably and append-only from the first write
anti_rework_rules.prevents: overwritten prior values that make rollback and audit impossible

anti_rework_rules.rule: Stage batch corrections as reviewable branches, never live bulk edits
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a systematic model error sweeping the whole graph before it is caught

anti_rework_rules.rule: Carry the retrieved evidence chunk into every proposal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: trust-the-model reviews that must be redone once the evidence is demanded

anti_rework_rules.rule: Defer schema legality and render to kgraph and viz from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: kb3 deciding a schema or render question it does not own and colliding with the siblings

iteration_protocol.trigger: the app's correction/provenance store is confirmed or specified by recon
iteration_protocol.action: bind the required PROV-O fields to the confirmed store and replace the UNKNOWN persistence note

iteration_protocol.trigger: an owner accepts or rejects a proposal
iteration_protocol.action: append the decision as an immutable record and update the edge's honesty tag accordingly

iteration_protocol.trigger: a human confirms a machine-corrected ESTIMATE edge
iteration_protocol.action: append a human-confirmation record and promote the honesty tag to FACT

iteration_protocol.trigger: kgraph rules on the legality of a proposed reverse/retype/add
iteration_protocol.action: finalize or withdraw the proposal according to the schema decision

iteration_protocol.trigger: a batch correction pass proves systematically unreliable
iteration_protocol.action: discard the whole branch and record the rejection rather than committing any of it

iteration_protocol.trigger: a real negated edge appears or viz ships the negation render contract
iteration_protocol.action: exercise the negate operation on real data and align with the render contract

iteration_protocol.trigger: the append-only ledger grows beyond a storage bound
iteration_protocol.action: add a retention/compaction policy that preserves prior values needed for rollback

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
18-21 nodes, 36-42 edges, 8-9 conflict_axes, 11-12 edge_cases, 10-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run

validation_report.notes: built by kgverify KB generator; run validators/kb_validator.py --mode dense to certify

test_cases.input_summary: smallest meaningful instance in this domain

evaluation_suite.regression_policy: re-run evaluation suite after any node addition or formula change
